title: State Visibility
summary: State visibility describes whether users can read the current condition of a system, its components, and in some cases the state of information or transactions. It is especially important in complex, high-consequence systems where multiple states change independently and operational decisions depend on rapid state verification.
keyFacts: State visibility is the degree to which users can determine current system activity without active investigation or navigation away from the current task.
State visibility includes operational mode, active conditions, fault states, readiness level, and managed component status.
State visibility is a prerequisite for action because users who cannot read system state cannot know whether to act, how to act, or whether a prior action had the intended effect.
State visibility is not synonymous with operational clarity; operational clarity is broader and includes whether information is organised into an appropriate hierarchy for decisions.
State visibility is not the same as data availability because state data must be surfaced at the right visual level, through reliable channels, at the right moment.
State visibility is not a status bar or dashboard feature; it is a property of the interface as a whole.
Effective state visibility requires readability under operating conditions, spatial consistency, and redundant communication channels.
Complex systems make state visibility harder because many component states can be active at the same time and may transition independently of user action.
The Torqeedo maritime HMI case recorded 50% faster energy state identification in a controlled experiment with 24 subjects and glance reduction in eye tracking with 7 subjects during sea trials.
The Kardion MCS Controller case used a layout stability standard derived from a clinical state visibility requirement; the available evidence is formative evaluation only.
KISPE Space illustrates information state as separate from device state, including record origin, age, delivery, and user visibility.
Schone Airspace Group illustrates transaction state as a third kind of state alongside device state and information state.

bodySections.heading: State Visibility Definition
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
State visibility is the degree to which users can determine what the system is currently doing without active investigation or navigation away from the current task. It includes operational mode, active conditions, fault states, readiness level, and the status of the components the system is managing.

State visibility is a prerequisite for action. Users who cannot read system state cannot know whether to act, how to act, or whether a prior action had the intended effect. In high-consequence and time-pressured contexts, state visibility is the condition that makes correct operational decisions possible.

bodySections.heading: State Visibility in Complex Operational Interfaces
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
In Creative Navy's documentation, state visibility refers to the interface property that makes current system condition legible at the point of use. The term is applied to complex systems such as medical devices, maritime vessels, industrial control systems, and multi-role enterprise platforms.

State visibility becomes an architectural problem when a system has many simultaneously active states across multiple components. In those contexts, the interface must maintain a legible picture of the system without overloading users with detail that they are not currently using.

bodySections.heading: Requirements for Effective State Visibility
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Effective state visibility requires readability under operating conditions. State indicators must remain communicable under divided attention, time pressure, variable lighting, physical movement, and gloved-hand use. A state indicator that is readable in a quiet office may be unreadable under operating theatre lighting or on a rolling vessel in heavy weather.

Effective state visibility requires spatial consistency. State indicators must remain in the same spatial position across view changes, modes, and workflow transitions. Spatial memory makes glance-readable state possible; if indicators move, users must search for state information at the moment they most need it.

Effective state visibility requires redundant communication channels. Critical state should be communicated through multiple simultaneous channels such as spatial position, icon form, and colour. Redundancy prevents the failure of a single channel from removing the signal under variable lighting, noise, vibration, or other degrading conditions.

bodySections.heading: How State Visibility Differs From Operational Clarity and Data Availability
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
State visibility is not the same as operational clarity. Operational clarity is broader: it concerns whether users can understand information and act on it without unnecessary cognitive translation. State visibility is the subset that concerns what the system is currently doing. A system with good state visibility communicates current condition clearly; operational clarity also requires the communication to be organised into an appropriate hierarchy for decisions.

State visibility is not the same as data availability. A system can hold complete state data and still have poor state visibility if that data is buried in a secondary screen or depends on a single communication channel that fails under operating conditions.

State visibility is not a status bar, dashboard, or specific user-interface component. An interface can contain a dedicated status bar and still have poor state visibility if the bar sits outside the primary visual field, fails under divided attention, or depends only on colour.

bodySections.heading: Device State, Information State, Transaction State, and Knowledge State
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
State visibility can apply to several kinds of state. Device state concerns the current condition of equipment, components, operating modes, readiness levels, and faults. In multi-component systems, device state may need to show several active conditions at once rather than reduce them to a single general status.

Information state concerns the condition of information itself. KISPE Space illustrates this distinction through information properties such as where a record came from, how old it was, whether it was delivered, and whether the user could see it. In this account, KISPE Space has no AI; the unknowns are properties of sources, links, protocols, and sensors.

Transaction state concerns the lifecycle of an action or command. Schone Airspace Group illustrates transaction state through commands that may be requested, acknowledged, and executed or not. That lifecycle is neither the state of the aircraft nor the state of the data about it.

Knowledge state concerns how firmly a system knows something. The maritime VTS engagement kept vessel identity, tracked object, and timestamped observations as separate objects, so the interface could show what was known, how it was known, and how firmly it was known.

bodySections.heading: Case Examples of State Visibility Design
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
The Torqeedo maritime HMI case illustrates device and component state visibility in a multi-component energy system. Propulsion, battery, and generation state were unified into a single coherent display with stable spatial positions and synchronised update cadences.

The Kardion MCS Controller case illustrates clinical state visibility through layout stability. The layout stability standard specified that no element shifts position across any view transition, because surgeons build spatial memory during procedures and depend on stable positions for rapid state verification.

The deSoutter Medical case illustrates redundant non-colour cues for critical device states. Critical states used spatial position, icon form, and colour because variable theatre lighting can degrade single-channel colour communication.

KISPE Space illustrates information state as separate from device state. Status was specified as seven independent dimensions rather than one green-to-red health score, because the single-score alternative would make identical colours carry conflicting meanings across domains.

Schone Airspace Group illustrates transaction state as a third kind of state alongside device state and information state. The interface preserves command transaction semantics as a visible object so an operator can distinguish what has been asked, what has been acknowledged, and what has been observed to happen.

bodySections.heading: Boundaries of the State Visibility Concept
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
State visibility should not be treated as proof that an interface is operationally clear. Operational clarity includes state visibility but also requires appropriate information hierarchy for the decisions that need to be made.

State visibility should not be inferred from the presence of a dashboard, status bar, colour code, or complete internal data model. The interface must surface state in a way that remains readable under actual operating conditions.

State visibility is a glossary concept. It describes a property of an interface and the conditions that make that property useful; it is not, by itself, a measured outcome.

Effective state visibility requires readability under operating conditions, spatial consistency, and redundant communication channels.

The Kardion MCS Controller layout stability standard was derived from a clinical state visibility requirement, and the available evidence is formative evaluation only.
KISPE Space illustrates information state as separate from device state through seven independent status dimensions rather than a single green-to-red health score.
Schone Airspace Group illustrates transaction state as a third kind of state alongside device state and information state.

weakerClaims: The deSoutter Medical case used redundant non-colour cues for critical device states because variable theatre lighting degrades single-channel colour-based communication.
limitations: State visibility is a glossary concept and should not be treated as a measured outcome by itself.
The Torqeedo evidence is the only example in the source with measured improvement claims.
The Kardion MCS Controller evidence is formative evaluation only; summative validation is the manufacturer's responsibility.
The deSoutter Medical evidence is surgeon-reported from design review sessions, not presented as an independently measured outcome.
KISPE Space, Schone Airspace Group, and the maritime VTS engagement describe design decisions and state models, not measured results.
KISPE Space has no AI in this account and should not be represented as a model, inference, or recommendation system.
The Schone Airspace Group product was built and is in test, not deployed.
Creative Navy did not support the KISPE Space build and has not compared the built interface against the delivered designs.
